summary: A square brick tower rising through a square keeper's house on a rock at the mouth of Frenchman Bay, lit in 1875 and still active.

notes_for_editor: No Light-House Board reports before 1891 are in the corpus, so the 1875 construction and 1876 gale rest on LighthouseFriends and New England Lighthouses (both modern, copyrighted; paraphrased). The 1900 and 1901 Board reports give scan pages only; printed page not checked. Fiscal-year reports: the 1900 report covers July 1899 to June 1900 (March 1900 storm fits). Lens characteristic after 1901 disputed (LighthouseFriends white flash vs New England Lighthouses flashing red); current record says Fl R 5s. Dalzell death: month (Feb vs Mar), body recovery (July vs 'over a month later') and who he was visiting differ between Lighthouse Digest and LighthouseFriends; only agreed points are stated and neither is a contemporary record (no 1935 newspaper read). Bulletin 1927/1929 rescues: the event year inside each volume was not confirmed (the Aug 3 and Oct 30 dates come from the volumes' commendation columns; the 1927 volume column text is interleaved with a neighbouring column by OCR, the Pinkham sentence matched by position). Hamor/Pinkham roles match the USLHS roster for those years. The 1904 Kennebec notice gives wrong coordinates for Egg Rock (44 31 N, 69 09 W) and was not used for position. Joseph Pulitzer's complaints (LighthouseFriends/NEL) are not in the story because the 1904 papers read do not name him. USLHS lists John W. Faulkingham, Kittila, Benjamin 'at least' dates; Coast Guard crew rows from 1960 are listed by the archive as 'other' with no position. Thomas L. Keene is from LighthouseFriends only. NRHP listing year (record says 1988) not verified: form was received Dec 1987.
